mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% signals a tightening cycle that increases discount rates, lowering the present value of future equity cash flows and thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 4% for 30 consecutive months, or IC > 0.05 over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the 6-month moving average of CPIAUCSL exceeds 253, the expectation of future inflation pushes the S&P 500 forward returns into a negative territory over the next 60 days due to equity valuation adjustments.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by UNRATE falling below 4% suggests a strengthening labor market that raises productivity expectations, pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns to the positive.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite the trigger, or the interaction p-value exceeds 0.10 in a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in GDPC1 (goods orders) followed by a rebound above the prior month's level indicates a turning point in business demand, which often precedes a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 drops >15% in a month then recovers above previous month's value
failure_condition: 5-day returns remain negative even after the rebound, or the signal is not confirmed by three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls for two consecutive months below its 50th percentile, it reflects supply-side weakness that tends to depress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during the contraction phase.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (new job creation) over the prior 10 trading days is a leading indicator of economic momentum that correlates with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative despite the interaction signal.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of FEDFUNDS below 2%, the lower real interest rates encourage risk-taking among investors, elevating S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average when the policy is in place.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of RSAFS (retail sales) falls below 500 billion dollars, it indicates softening consumer demand which typically results in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite RSAFS in contraction phase.
